overall_summary: Analysis of 15 recent Shorts shows top performance driven by curiosity-focused space and animal trivia ('What Color Is a Sunset on Mars?' at 450 views and 'Which animal is known for changing its skin color...' at 383 views, 25 likes, and 1 subscriber). Average view percentage peaked at 75.68% on concise, clear geography trivia ('Which is the largest ocean on Earth?'). Conversely, five recent uploads currently have 0 recorded views, and question history shows repeated recycling of identical concepts (e.g., optical illusion lines, Greek inventions, and landmark dates). Confidence remains low due to zero measured strategy outcomes in history.

winning_patterns.pattern: Curiosity gap astronomy and surprising natural science questions
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What Color Is a Sunset on Mars?' generated the channel high of 450 views, 53 estimated minutes watched, and 1 subscriber. 'Only sharp minds get this one! Which planet has the most prominent ring system?' earned 234 views and 17 likes.
winning_patterns.action: Prioritize vivid planetary and space perception questions featuring unexpected facts and crisp multi-choice options.

winning_patterns.pattern: Concise, high-clarity trivia with strong pacing
winning_patterns.evidence: 'Quick geography challenge! Which is the largest ocean on Earth?' achieved the highest average view percentage (75.68%) and average view duration (26s), maintaining 0.7674 audience watch ratio at 0.49 video progress.
winning_patterns.action: Maintain short, direct question setups with immediately visible A/B/C/D prompts to sustain audience watch ratio above 1.0 in the first 5 seconds.

improvements.pattern: Direct repetition of identical trivia prompts
improvements.evidence: Question history reveals verbatim or near-verbatim duplication of questions (Müller-Lyer lines 3 times, ancient Greek inventions 4 times, landmark construction dates 3 times, country with most volcanoes 2 times).
improvements.action: Enforce strict deduplication in topic selection; replace repeated questions with fresh, unexplored domain-specific paradoxes.

improvements.pattern: Zero-view publishing stall on consecutive uploads
improvements.evidence: The 5 most recent videos published between 2026-09-11 and 2026-09-13 show 0 views, 0 likes, and 0 comments.
improvements.action: Realign release schedules to proven engagement windows (12:05 UTC and 15:15 UTC) and avoid rapid back-to-back uploads with generic fallback titles.

retention_insights.video_pattern: Early-second audience retention drop-off on complex logic puzzles
retention_insights.evidence: 'The Flying Bird Physics Puzzle' showed a steep relative retention drop (starting at 0.1933 relative retention at 0.01 progress and dropping to 0.0494 at 0.49 progress, averaging 48.1% APV).
retention_insights.action: Ensure the visual clue and question hook are instantly decodable within 1.5 seconds rather than requiring abstract mental modeling.

retention_insights.video_pattern: High initial re-watch and hook retention on visual trivia
retention_insights.evidence: 'Quick geography challenge! Which is the largest ocean on Earth?' achieved an initial audience watch ratio of 1.2093 and relative retention of 0.6052, retaining 0.7674 watch ratio at mid-video (0.49 progress).
retention_insights.action: Lead with bold, full-screen graphical contrast and high-stakes visual options right at progress 0.00.

best_posting_windows.reason: The channel's highest-viewed video ('What Color Is a Sunset on Mars?', 450 views, 53 estimated minutes watched) was published at 12:05 UTC.
The top-converting video for engagement ('Which animal is known for changing its skin color...', 383 views, 25 likes, 1 comment, 1 subscriber) was published at 15:16 UTC.
